blogs.title: From LSTM to xLSTM: Can RNNs Power the Next Wave of Language Models?
blogs.description: A big-picture tour of why the authors revisit LSTMs in the transformer era, the three classic LSTM pain points (revising memory, storage capacity, and parallelism), and how xLSTM answers them with exponential gates, a new scalar variant (sLSTM), and a matrix-memory variant (mLSTM). Includes a plain-English summary of what changes and why it matters.

blogs.title: Exponential Gating, Simply Explained: How xLSTM Learns to Rewrite Its Own Memories
blogs.description: An intuitive guide to xLSTM’s exponential input and forget gates and why they let the model revise earlier storage decisions—something classic LSTMs struggle with. Covers the role of the normalizer and stabilizer states (to keep numbers sane) and uses an everyday analogy to show how the mechanism outperforms standard gating on tasks like nearest-neighbor updates.

blogs.title: Matrix Memory in Plain English: mLSTM’s Built-In Key–Value Store
blogs.description: Demystifies the mLSTM cell, which replaces a single scalar cell state with a full matrix that stores key–value pairs, enabling stronger recall of rare or numerous facts. Explains associative memory and the covariance update rule in practical terms, how retrieval works with queries, and the trade-off between huge capacity and higher compute—plus why it still runs efficiently on GPUs.

blogs.title: Why sLSTM Still Matters: Memory Mixing, Heads, and Real State Tracking
blogs.description: Zooms in on the sLSTM variant with exponential gates and memory mixing across cells (and within heads). Explains why this gives xLSTM real state-tracking ability that many state-space and attention-only models lack, and uses formal-language tasks like parity to show where sLSTM shines.

blogs.title: Inside an xLSTM Block: Residual Backbones Without the Attention Tax
blogs.description: Breaks down the xLSTM residual blocks, including pre- and post-up-projection paths inspired by modern LLM design. Explains, without equations, how nonlinearly summarizing history in higher dimensions (a nod to Cover’s theorem) improves separability of contexts, and how stacking these blocks builds full xLSTM architectures.

blogs.title: Speed, Memory, and Context: How xLSTM Competes with Transformers and SSMs
blogs.description: Translates the paper’s engineering claims into practical expectations: linear-time, constant-memory decoding; why xLSTM can handle longer contexts and larger batches; and where it currently lags (e.g., sLSTM parallelism and mLSTM compute). Summarizes generation throughput comparisons and why edge deployments may benefit.

blogs.title: Do xLSTMs Scale? What the 15B and 300B Token Results Really Say
blogs.description: A tour of the experiments: validation perplexity on SlimPajama, downstream task scores, PALOMA’s 571 domains, and length extrapolation up to 16k. Interprets the scaling-law plots in plain language and distills the takeaways: xLSTM’s consistent edge over leading baselines and what that implies for larger models.

blogs.title: Where xLSTM Fits in the Model Zoo: RWKV, Mamba, Retention, and Beyond
blogs.description: Positions xLSTM among recent RNNs and linear-attention models, clarifying overlaps (gating, associative updates) and crucial differences (exponential gating with mixing, matrix memory with normalization). Offers a buyer’s guide perspective on when to favor xLSTM versus Transformers, SSMs, or other RNNs.
